_doc: Dimensions the concept dice draws from. Each option: id, label, how (one-line production note). Add options freely; ids must stay unique and stable because the ledger stores them.

mechanism.label: Visual metaphor - fusion
mechanism.how: Product merges with the source-domain object (can = dumbbell, serum = morning sun).

mechanism.label: Visual metaphor - replacement
mechanism.how: Product sits where the expected object should be; the viewer completes the meaning.

mechanism.label: Visual metaphor - transformation
mechanism.how: The product CAUSES the world to change state on screen.

mechanism.label: Extreme attribute
mechanism.how: Push one true product attribute to an absurd, visible extreme.

mechanism.label: Extreme / inverted consequence
mechanism.how: Show what happens downstream of using (or not using) it, exaggerated.

mechanism.label: Competition - uncommon use
mechanism.how: The product wins in a contest it was never designed for.

mechanism.label: Dimensionality - scale
mechanism.how: Giant product in a real place, or tiny people in a product world.

mechanism.label: Dimensionality - time leap
mechanism.how: Compress years into seconds, or slow one second into ten.

mechanism.label: Insight - confess a flaw
mechanism.how: Admit a real weakness and turn it into the proof.

mechanism.label: Insight - name the enemy
mechanism.how: Personify the problem/habit the audience hates (not a competitor).

mechanism.label: Insight - say the unsaid
mechanism.how: Voice the thought the audience has but never says out loud.

mechanism.label: AI spectacle - impossible camera
mechanism.how: One continuous move through places a camera cannot go.

mechanism.label: AI spectacle - one physics law broken
mechanism.how: Exactly one law breaks (gravity, liquid, time) and the product causes it.

mechanism.label: Recurring character / world
mechanism.how: A character or world that can run 10+ episodes and becomes a brand asset.

format.label: Nature documentary
format.how: Hushed narrator studies the product/customer as a wild species.

format.label: Heist
format.how: Crew plans and executes stealing the product; cut on beats.

format.label: ASMR macro
format.how: Extreme macro textures + crisp foley, no VO.

format.label: POV
format.how: First-person, text hook 'POV: ...', handheld feel added in post.

format.label: Mock luxury
format.how: Perfume-ad grandeur applied to an everyday product.

format.label: Sports broadcast
format.how: Play-by-play commentary + replay + stats lower-thirds (added in post).

format.label: Weather / news report
format.how: Anchor treats the product/benefit as breaking local news.

format.label: True crime
format.how: Evidence board, reenactment, the product is the suspect or the alibi.

format.label: Infomercial parody
format.how: Black-and-white 'there has to be a better way' then colour payoff.

format.label: Museum exhibit
format.how: The product displayed and studied as a priceless artifact.

format.label: Cooking show
format.how: Recipe format where the product is the hero ingredient or the tool.

format.label: Video game
format.how: Power-up, level-up, inventory UI added in post over cinematic footage.

format.label: Blocks to reality
format.how: Blender blockout morphs into the real world (reel-studio reveal).

format.label: One continuous take
format.how: Single unbroken camera journey, product appears at the end state.

format.label: Stop-motion / claymation look
format.how: Stylised handmade world; hides AI imperfections, high charm.

format.label: Split-screen compare
format.how: Two lives side by side, one with the product (no unsubstantiated claims).

format.label: Music video
format.how: Cut entirely to a beat; the product moves on downbeats.

format.label: Silent film
format.how: Title cards, over-cranked motion, piano; nostalgic and funny.

format.label: Mock-doc interview
format.how: Talking-head of an object, pet or fictional expert (never a fake customer testimonial).

format.label: FOOH (fake out-of-home)
format.how: Impossible billboard/street stunt in a recognisable real place, labelled as AI.

format.label: Prompt reveal
format.how: Show the text prompt typing, then the shot appears - meta, creator-native.

format.label: Dream / daydream
format.how: Mundane moment drifts into a surreal product world and snaps back.

format.label: Epic unboxing
format.how: Opening the package releases a world, scaled up cinematically.

format.label: Perfect loop
format.how: Last frame equals first frame; drives rewatches.

hook.label: Visual anomaly
hook.how: Frame 1 shows something that should not exist.

hook.label: Payoff first
hook.how: Open on the most satisfying frame, then rewind.

hook.label: Text tension
hook.how: On-screen line that creates an open loop (sound-off proof).

hook.label: Sound-led
hook.how: A distinctive sound in the first 0.3 s before the image explains it.

hook.label: Scale shock
hook.how: The product is wildly the wrong size in frame 1.

hook.label: Wrong answer
hook.how: Start doing it the wrong/funny way; viewers stay to see it fixed.

hook.label: Confession
hook.how: 'We have to admit something...' as super or VO.

hook.label: Countdown / stakes
hook.how: A timer or stakes established in 1 s.

hook.label: Direct question
hook.how: A question the target audience answers 'yes' to in their head.

hook.label: Mid-action
hook.how: Start in the middle of motion (pour, splash, fall).

structure.label: List of 3 (rule of three, twist on 3rd)

look.label: Hard tropical sun, saturated teal and coral

constraint: The product is never shown whole until the last 2 seconds.
Tell it from the product's point of view.
No people's faces - only hands, silhouettes or backs.
The first 3 seconds have no product and no logo - only the problem.
Every shot must contain the brand colour.
The ad must make sense with the sound off AND with the screen off (VO only).
Set it somewhere it has never been advertised (a laundromat, a courtroom, the moon).
The hero is the least likely customer.
Use the packaging itself as the set.
Reverse the expected emotion of the category (a calm energy drink, a loud perfume).
Make it a loop: the last frame is the first frame.
The product appears in every shot but is the focus of only one.
Shoot it as if it were a 1950s ad, but the product is modern.
The punchline is a sound, not a picture.
Something must go wrong on screen and the product saves it.
Use one real filmed shot (phone) and only AI for the rest.
